cards.title: Introduction to Python Automation
cards.content:
Automation is the use of software and scripts to perform repetitive, manual tasks without human intervention.

Python is the premier language for automation due to its rich ecosystem of libraries and readable syntax.

import time
print('Starting automated task...')
time.sleep(1)
print('Task complete!')

cards.title: File and Directory Management
cards.content:
Python's built-in os and shutil modules allow you to automate file organization, renaming, and moving.

import os
import shutil

# Create a directory
os.makedirs('backup', exist_ok=True)

# Move a file
shutil.move('data.txt', 'backup/data.txt')

cards.title: Choose the best library for file operations
Web Scraping & Browser Automation
cards.content:
Web automation involves extracting data from websites or interacting with web pages programmatically.

Libraries like BeautifulSoup parse HTML, while Selenium controls a real web browser to click buttons and fill forms.

from selenium import webdriver

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
driver.get('https://example.com')
# Automate interactions here
driver.quit()

cards.title: Error Handling in Automation
cards.content:
Automated scripts often run unattended. Robust error handling ensures your script fails gracefully or retries when network issues or missing files occur.

try:
    os.remove('temp.log')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print('File already deleted or missing.')

cards.title: Why is exception handling critical in automation?

options.text: It makes the code run twice as fast.
It prevents unattended scripts from crashing unexpectedly.
It automatically writes unit tests for you.
It eliminates the need for variables.

cards.title: Summary and Next Steps
cards.content:
You have explored the core components of Python automation: file handling, web tools, scheduling, and error management.

Start small by automating a tedious daily task, like organizing your downloads folder!
